chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Ziyad ibn Sūqah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): Is there a limit for breastfeeding that is taken into account? He said: Breastfeeding does not prohibit (marriage) for less than breastfeeding for a day and a night, or fifteen consecutive sucklings from one mother, from the milk of one male (animal), without being interrupted by sucklings from another mother. And if a mother breastfed a boy or a girl ten sucklings from the milk of one male, and another mother breastfed her ten sucklings from the milk of another male, the marriage would not be prohibited.

key_terms.فَحْلٍ: Male (animal), referring to the source of the milk

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of breastfeeding required to make marriage prohibited in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the precise quantitative and qualitative criteria for establishing *mahramiyyah* through breastfeeding, specifying a minimum of a day and a night or fifteen consecutive sucklings from a single mother. Crucially, the ruling emphasizes continuity; if the nursing is interrupted by sucklings from another woman, the threshold is reset, ensuring the prohibition applies only to direct, uninterrupted nursing from one source. This hadith serves as a foundational text in Shia jurisprudence for resolving disputes regarding kinship ties (*silat al-rahim*) and marital eligibility based on wet-nursing history.
